messages:
maria: Heads-up — started seeing a cluster-wide uptick in soft-429s on /v1/generate around 02:10 UTC after the kernel-hint flip. Patterns look like batch size oscillation + high KV prefetch contention. I can pull logs if useful.

ken: Can you paste a short diff of p95/p99 and a representative log line?

maria: quick log sample:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:12Z] service=runtime admit=soft429 reason=\"batch-oscillation\" kernel_hint=\"fused_bias\" batch_size=4->12 kv_prefetch_ratio=0.82 pool=dedicated-us-east-1
```
p95 latency for that pool jumped ~18% and p99 ~35% during the window.

sam: That log line and the numbers smell like the batcher is flipping kernels mid-assembly which increases assembly latency and causes token_budget to get exhausted then soft-shed. My profiling run earlier showed per-batch kernel selection_count spiking when KV prefetch > ~0.6.

nina: Any correlation with sequence lengths or client route patterns? Could be a short-seq-heavy burst causing small batches that then get coalesced incorrectly.

maria: We saw a mode where incoming seq_len distribution had a lot of 8-16 token requests. Kernel hint favored a low-overhead kernel for those, but once a larger request entered the window the batcher attempted to switch, causing a pause. KV prefetch kept filling the allocator which amplified the latency.

ken: Proposal for immediate mitigation: temporarily cap token_budget_target for affected pool and disable KV prefetch for the route to reduce allocator pressure. That should drop the oscillation while we tune the heuristic.

sam: Agreed. Also add short-term telemetry: expose metric `runtime.batch.kernel_flip_rate` and `runtime.batcher.batch_size_by_kernel` so we can see flip correlation.

maria: Applying patch to canary now:
```
# temporary canary override
pool.overrides.dedicated-us-east-1.batcher:
  token_budget_target: 512
  kv_prefetch_enabled: false
```
Will roll to 5% canary.

ci-bot: canary deploy started for commit a3f4b2 (maria) — canary=5%

ken: If you see improvement, we should keep as a bandaid and then iterate on the batching heuristic. Longer-term: prefer kernel-selection stability over aggressive single-request speed if it causes assembly churn. Maybe a hysteresis window on kernel choice per-assembly.

sam: Notes from profiling: kernel selection currently uses a soft score that doesn't account for in-flight KV allocation. Idea: subtract a penalty proportional to current kv_prefetch_ratio so the kernel selector prefers the more stable kernel when prefetch is high. Also consider lowering target batch assembly timeout when flip_rate > threshold.

nina: Sounds reasonable. Can we prepare an A/B to verify? A: kv-penalty heuristic, B: assembly-timeout shrink. We'll check error rates and cost.

maria: Canary metrics: soft-429 rate on canary pool down by ~70% at 5% after 6 minutes, p95 latency back to baseline. Rolling to 25% now. :thumbsup:

ken: Good. Create a short follow-up perf run plan and include synthetic workload that reproduces the seq_len skew + high prefetch. Add perf notes to the ticket.

sam: I'll own the perf run. Plan: 3 experiments — baseline (current prod), patched-token_budget, and patched-kv-penalty; for each sweep seq_len distributions [8,16,64] and prefetch ratios [0.2,0.6,0.9]. Collect per-kernel latency, kernel_flip_rate, and batch_size_hist.

maria: Filing a ticket and linking results here. If the heuristic change (kv-penalty) looks good and doesn't regress single-request p50, we can bake it. Otherwise keep the token_budget cap as fallback.

nina: Thanks everyone — keeping an eye on this. If anything spikes, I'll trigger emergency rollback on the kernel-hint change.

maria: Updated last: canary -> 25%, soft-429s reduced, will continue monitoring. cc @ken @sam @nina
